    01

    Choose an agent

    Choose the page that matches your task. Both pages use the same local API and configured model.

    Use this comparison before you start.
    AgentUse it forHow files change
    General assistantExplain attached files. Create Word documents, spreadsheets, slides, or PDFs. Analyze data. Create small utilities.The agent writes to the chat workspace. Commands run automatically. Completed turns retain file versions.
    Coding workbenchInspect a local repository. Plan a change. Edit code. Run checks. Inspect a diff.The agent works in a separate copy. You select files and apply a reviewed revision to the original.

    For a document task

    Use General assistant when the output is a file or an explanation of supplied data.

    Example: “Inspect this spreadsheet. Create a summary of missing values and duplicate records.”

    For a code task

    Use Coding workbench when the change belongs in an existing repository and needs tests and review.

    Example: “Add input validation to the import function. Keep the existing behavior for valid files.”

    This report is a guide.
    Its buttons search, copy, print, or open diagrams. They do not run agent tasks or change repository files.

    Source: application page selection · product behavior.

    02

    Start the application

    Complete the operator setup once. Use the launcher for the basic workflow.

    Required

    Local software

    Use macOS or Linux with Python 3.11–3.14 and uv.

    Required

    Model access

    Configure a LangChain model that supports tool calls. Add its provider credential to .env.

    Task dependent

    Document tools

    Node.js/npm supports Office file creation. LibreOffice and Poppler support file rendering. Tesseract enables local OCR.

    1. Open a terminal in the application folder.

      Use the general-agent folder, not the repository that you want the coding agent to edit.

      Application folder on this computer
      cd /Users/charlie/Repos/deepagents-agents/general-agent
    2. If .env does not exist, copy .env.example to .env.

      Keep an existing configuration. Do not replace it with this example.

      First setup only
      cp .env.example .env
    3. Set MODEL_NAME in .env.

      Use the provider-qualified model name that your provider supports.

    4. Add the required provider credential to .env.

      Keep credentials out of task messages, source files, and editor settings. Model calls can incur provider charges.

    5. Confirm that CODING_RUNTIME=local is set.

      Local is also the default when this setting is absent. Docker is not required.

    6. Run the launcher.
      Start the API and user interface
      ./scripts/start.sh

      The launcher synchronizes locked dependencies and checks the configuration, ports, and API health.

    7. Open http://127.0.0.1:8502.

      Select General assistant or Coding workbench in the application navigation.

    The project includes the OpenAI provider adapter. Other providers can require an additional operator-managed adapter.

    Readiness checks configuration and service health. It does not verify model access, credentials, or available provider credit.

    Existing exported variables take precedence over .env. Restart the application from a terminal with the intended settings.

    Check the main settings
    SettingUse
    MODEL_NAMERequired model identifier. The application passes it to LangChain.
    MODEL_KWARGS_JSONOptional provider settings. Enclose JSON in single quotes for the shell launcher.
    DEFAULT_CORP_IDSelects the local corporation namespace. It is not a password or authentication method.
    API_HOST / APP_HOSTKeep loopback addresses. Defaults: 127.0.0.1.
    API_PORT / APP_PORTDefaults: 8001 / 8502. Keep API_BASE_URL consistent.
    JSON quoting example · no credentials
    MODEL_KWARGS_JSON='{}'
CODING_RUNTIME=local
API_HOST=127.0.0.1
APP_HOST=127.0.0.1

    Stop or restart the application.
    Press Ctrl + C in the launcher terminal to stop both services. Restart after configuration changes.

    The standard launcher does not retain the optional browser extra. Use the browser startup procedure when browser checks are required.

    Source: launcher · configuration example · validated settings.

    03

    Use the General assistant

    Describe the result, supply the input, and inspect the output. The agent can plan and delegate parts of the task.

    SidebarNew chatWorkspaceCurrent chat / SharedAdd files
    Work with files, code, and plans

    Describe your output and attach files in the message composer.

    Message General Agent or attach files
    Plan and activityStopFiles from this turn

    Screen map. This is a guide illustration, not a live application screen.

    Complete a file task

    1. Select General assistant.

      The page restores its current chat from the local URL.

    2. Attach the input files in the message composer.

      Alternatively, use Workspace → Add files → Upload. Common types include PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, and text.

    3. Enter a task with a clear output.

      Include the file name, purpose, format, and required checks.

    4. Submit the message.

      The agent works automatically. A starter example fills the composer but does not submit it.

    5. Inspect the plan and activity.

      The activity shows tool work, commands, and delegation. The final answer appears when the run completes.

    6. Open Files from this turn.

      This section lists retained file versions from that turn.

    7. Select Download for the required file.

      Inspect the file before you use or share it.

    Example request · spreadsheet
    Inspect sales.xlsx. Identify missing values and duplicate records. Create summary.xlsx with the findings. Check the output workbook.
    Replace the file name with your attachment.
    Example request · document
    Read the attached project notes. Create a Word project brief with scope, owners, risks, and next steps. Render and inspect the document.
    Supply the source notes with the request.

    Keep a file across chats

    1. Open the file's Actions menu.
    2. Select Keep in shared.
    3. Select Shared in Workspace.

    The Shared area persists across chats in the same corporation namespace. Refer to the file explicitly in a later task.

    Start a fresh chat

    1. Wait for the current run to finish.
    2. Select New chat.
    3. Enter the next task.

    The browser shows one chat at a time. There is no chat picker. A saved conversation URL can restore that chat.

    Inspect, rename, download, or delete a workspace file

    Select a file name for its preview. Use Actions for Preview, Download, Rename, or Delete.

    Some file types show extracted text or metadata. A preview is not a complete visual check of an Office document.

    Clean up chat files removes the chat's live files after confirmation. Retained turn versions remain available. Shared files remain unchanged.

    Choose the correct document request
    Input or outputUseful requestRequired check
    PDFSummarize specified pages. Cite the page for each finding.Inspect embedded text and the relevant pages. Scanned pages need OCR software.
    Word documentCreate or revise a document from supplied notes.Render the pages and inspect the layout.
    PowerPoint slidesCreate a deck for a named audience and purpose.Render the slides and inspect text, spacing, and overlap.
    SpreadsheetAnalyze supplied data. Create formulas and a stated summary.Recalculate formulas and inspect errors and outputs.

    Report missing renderers or OCR tools explicitly. A supplied file does not prove that its complete content was read.

    The upload picker accepts supported text, source, PDF, and Office formats. It does not accept images, audio, or archives.

    Download original retrieves an attached original. Workspace Download retrieves a live file. Turn Download retrieves that turn's retained version.

    Stop a task or inspect a failed result
    1. Select Stop in the active run.
    2. Wait for the run to show a stopped state.
    3. Inspect available files and activity.
    4. Send a new request when you are ready to continue.

    A stopped run can contain partial files. Do not assume that a partial output passed its checks.

    Open How this was produced, Run diagnostics, or Technical details for additional information.

    The General assistant has no built-in web search, email, calendar, audio understanding, or conversation export.

    Source: General assistant controls · activity and downloads · document skills.

    04

    Use the Coding workbench

    Register a repository. Create a session. Request a plan or a change. The session contains a separate source copy.

    01 / REGISTERChoose the repository

    Set its folder and check commands.

    02 / PLANInspect the task

    Review the proposed work.

    03 / IMPLEMENTEdit and check the copy

    Inspect logs and the result.

    04 / APPLYReview selected files

    Apply the exact revision.

    Open a repository

    1. Select Coding workbench.

      Open Runtime and optional tools to inspect local readiness.

    2. Open Open a repository in the sidebar.
    3. Enter the Absolute repository folder.

      Use the real folder path of the target project. Save editor files before you create a session.

    4. Enter a Project name.
    5. Enter the Tests command.

      The default is python -m pytest. Choose a command that matches your repository and available tools.

    6. If a build check is required, enter the Build command (optional).

      These names and commands define the recorded checks. An assistant statement does not replace a recorded check.

    7. If public documentation is required, enter Documentation websites (optional).

      Enter exact hostnames separated by commas, such as docs.python.org. Do not enter full URLs.

    8. Select Open project.
    9. Select the registered Project.
    10. Select New coding session.

      The new session includes eligible source files and their current on-disk edits.

    11. Check the displayed original: folder beneath Coding session.

      The session selector includes all projects in the current namespace. The sidebar Project selection controls new-session creation.

    A session is a source snapshot.
    Later original-file edits do not refresh an existing session. Create a new session to work from the current on-disk source.

    Choose check commands carefully. The current product cannot edit a registered project's name or check commands.

    Reopening the same root keeps those values. A new session also keeps its project's check commands.

    Understand which files enter the session

    The copy uses ignore-aware source rules. It excludes protected secrets, symbolic links, dependency/build caches, and this application's runtime folders.

    Source size and file-count limits also apply. A new session does not copy an entire host directory without checks.

    Registration reports source counts, size, and exclusions. The current workbench screen does not display that report.

    General assistant attachments and Shared files do not automatically enter the coding copy.

    Ask the agent to inspect the relevant source paths before it proposes a change.

    Select a task mode

    The mode selector shows plan, implement, and review.
    ModeWhat it permitsUse it when
    planInspect source and propose work. Repository commands and source edits are unavailable.You want to agree on the scope before implementation.
    reviewInspect source and report findings. Repository commands and source edits are unavailable.You need an explanation or code review without a change.
    implementEdit the source copy. Run bounded commands and approved checks. Use available optional tools.You already know and authorize the required change.

    Run the first task

    1. Select plan in Task mode.
    2. Enter the request in Task.

      State the expected behavior, limits, and required checks.

    3. Select Start task.

      The queue permits one writer for each session.

    4. Read the completed plan.
    5. If the plan is correct, select Approve plan and implement.

      The approval binds implementation to the reviewed source revision.

    6. Inspect the implementation's logs and checks.
    7. Use the next chapter to review the diff.

    Select Reject plan if the plan is unsuitable. Start another plan task with the required correction.

    For direct implementation, select implement and Start task. This path does not require a separate plan approval.

    Example request · plan
    Inspect the CSV import function and its tests. Plan a fix for empty files. Describe the expected behavior and required tests.
    Use the plan mode.
    Example request · implement
    Reject empty CSV files with a clear error. Add a regression test. Run the approved tests check. Report remaining failures.
    Use implement only when the scope is clear.

    Answer a question

    1. Read the displayed question.
    2. Enter Your answer.
    3. Select Answer and resume.

    The task resumes its saved checkpoint with its remaining budgets.

    Steer active work

    1. Enter a Follow-up instruction.
    2. Select Queue follow-up.

    The instruction waits for the next writer boundary. It does not interrupt an active command immediately.

    Source: workbench controls · registered roots · source inventory · mode policy.

    05

    Review and apply a change

    Task completion and original-file application are separate actions. A completed task can still have failed or missing checks.

    Inspect the evidence first

    0 of 5 review checks selected. This checklist does not approve a change.
    Interpret a result before you apply it.
    Evidence or stateMeaningNext action
    Baseline failureThe check failed before the implementation changed the source.Separate existing failures from failures caused by the change.
    Final check passedThe recorded command passed for the observed source and environment.Inspect the check log and displayed status.
    verifiedAll required final checks have current passing evidence.Review the diff. Recheck the merged original after apply.
    checks_failedA required final check or browser check failed.Inspect its log and resolve the failure.
    Stale evidenceSource or dependencies changed after the check.Request new checks for the current state.
    not_verifiedThe required current evidence is missing, stale, or incomplete.Resolve the blocker. Do not treat a completed answer as verification.
    blockedA required runtime or setup prerequisite is unavailable.Resolve the displayed prerequisite before a new attempt.
    Browser screenshotThe private preview produced visual evidence for one page state.Inspect the image. Keep the required project checks.

    Apply selected files

    1. Open Review changes on the completed attempt.
    2. Read the diff for each changed file.
    3. Select the required files in Files to apply.

      The selection applies whole files. There is no line-by-line or hunk selection.

    4. Stop other edits to the original checkout.

      A separate editor does not share the application's writer lock.

    5. Select Apply selected files to original.

      The service checks the root identity, revision, and original file preimages before it writes.

    6. Inspect the original files after application.
    7. Run the required checks on the merged original.

      Copy verification becomes stale for the original after application. Partial application can produce a different combined source state.

    Reject an unapplied proposal

    1. Select Reject change proposal.
    2. Inspect the restored review copy.

    The session returns to its accepted baseline. The rejected proposal cannot be applied.

    Revert an application

    1. Open the applied change.
    2. Select Revert this application.
    3. Inspect the original files.

    Revert refuses to overwrite observed newer edits. It is not a general Git reset.

    Apply does not publish code.
    Apply does not commit, push, or create a pull request. GitHub publication requires its separate reviewed action.

    Source: review actions · immutable changes and apply checks · verification rules.

    06

    Prepare optional tools

    The basic local workflow does not need Docker, the TypeScript SDK, or a browser. Add tools when the task needs them.

    Prepare project dependencies

    1. Open Dependencies in the workbench.
    2. Read the locked files and blockers.

      Python accepts exact hash-pinned wheels or eligible uv.lock metadata. Node accepts eligible public package-lock.json files.

    3. Wait for active session work to finish.
    4. Select the available Prepare python dependencies or Prepare node dependencies button.

      Preparation downloads packages through fixed package-manager commands.

    5. Inspect the Dependency preparation log.

      Saved package artifacts install into private session folders. They do not install into the application's environment or global folders.

    6. Confirm that the dependency status shows prepared.
    7. Run the implementation or approved checks.

    Changed lockfiles or runtime identities invalidate preparation. Prepare the current dependencies before you use them.

    Private registries, local/workspace packages, editable packages, and source builds are unavailable in managed preparation.

    Node lifecycle scripts are disabled. Packages that require those scripts can remain unusable after preparation.

    Enable JavaScript and TypeScript navigation
    1. Open a terminal in the application folder.
    2. Install the pinned application SDK.
    TypeScript 5.9.3 · operator setup
    npm ci --prefix tooling/coding --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
    1. Restart the application.
    2. Inspect Runtime and optional tools.

    The default SDK path is tooling/coding/node_modules/typescript/lib/typescript.js.

    CODING_TYPESCRIPT_SDK can select another absolute path to the same version. Navigation does not load project plugins or tsconfig.json.

    Definitions and references cover bounded source snapshots and fixed SDK libraries. Package types and path aliases can remain unresolved.

    Enable browser checks without Docker

    Use the manual startup below for browser checks.
    The standard ./scripts/start.sh runs dependency sync without the browser extra. It can remove Playwright at the next start.

    1. Stop the application.
    2. Open a terminal in the application folder.
    3. Confirm that the system has lsof.
    4. Install the locked browser extra.
    Optional application dependencies
    uv sync --locked --all-groups --extra browser
    1. Install Chromium for the pinned Playwright version.
    Browser download · operator setup
    .venv/bin/python -m playwright install chromium
    1. Start the API in this terminal.
    Terminal 1 · default loopback API
    .venv/bin/uvicorn general_agent.api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --workers 1
    1. Open a second terminal in the application folder.
    2. Start the user interface in the second terminal.
    Terminal 2 · default loopback interface
    .venv/bin/streamlit run streamlit_app.py --server.address 127.0.0.1 --server.port 8502 --server.headless true
    1. Open the workbench.
    2. Confirm that Browser checks shows available.

    Both services load the application configuration. These examples use the default ports. Adjust the commands and API_BASE_URL together for other ports.

    Use one API worker. Press Ctrl + C in each terminal to stop manual startup.

    macOS includes lsof. Linux requires the system utility and Chromium's operating-system dependencies.

    Request a private preview

    Example request · implement
    Start a private preview on a free port. Bind it to 127.0.0.1. Check the heading on /. Capture a screenshot. Stop the preview.
    Use after browser readiness shows available.

    The agent starts previews through its tools. There is no separate user form to start a preview.

    Use Process panels to inspect output or select Stop process. Use Browser panels to inspect screenshots and reasons.

    Previews use their own source copies. Preview writes do not become source proposals. An occupied or unrelated listener is rejected.

    Source: dependency preparation · local runtime and readiness · navigation · preview lifecycle.

    07

    Explore the architecture

    Each diagram shows the current implementation. Use the viewer to inspect components and their relationships.

    Use the viewer's zoom controls to inspect labels. Open the full diagram for a larger workspace.

    The General assistant writes to scoped chat files and can execute host commands.

    The interactive diagrams are in the HTML report. The architecture summaries below also appear in this print view.

    General assistant

    Request → tools → files

    Streamlit sends the task and attachments to FastAPI. The run manager starts the DeepAgents graph and records progress.

    The graph uses the configured model, planning, skills, file tools, and delegated work. Shell commands run on the host.

    SQLite retains chat and run data. The workspace retains live files. Immutable turn versions support downloads after later file changes.

    Coding workbench

    Request → copy → reviewed apply

    The coding service registers roots, creates source copies, and schedules one writer per session.

    Plan and Review inspect source. Implement uses the selected runtime, tools, and check evidence. Local is the default.

    The change service freezes a revision and diff. An explicit reviewed action applies selected files to the registered original root.

    Model calls use the configured provider.
    The application runs locally, but configured model calls can send task content to the provider. Optional tracing can send tool data.

    The diagrams use Archify. Their final validation, hashes, and browser evidence are included in the report's artifact folder.

    Source: General agent graph · run manager · coding service · shared API.

    08

    Connect other services

    These capabilities are optional. Configure each capability for its intended purpose. Keep credentials in the application settings.

    Read approved public documentation
    1. Enter approved exact hostnames when you register the project.
    2. Ask the coding agent to consult those documentation sites.

    Without approved domains, the agent receives no documentation tools. The broker permits public HTTPS requests to the approved domains.

    Set BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY only when domain-scoped search is required. Search is optional.

    Documentation permission does not restrict local shell networking. Local project commands still have host permissions.

    Review and publish a draft GitHub pull request

    Operator setup

    1. Provision a repository-scoped GitHub token.
    2. Set GITHUB_TOKENS_JSON in .env.
    3. Restart the application.
    Template · replace the token outside this report
    GITHUB_TOKENS_JSON='{"A123456":"REPLACE_WITH_GITHUB_TOKEN"}'

    Read access needs repository and issue/PR permissions. Draft publication also needs content and pull-request write permissions.

    Workflow-file changes can require additional token permissions.

    Workbench actions

    1. Open GitHub.
    2. Enter GitHub owner and GitHub repository.
    3. Select Connect this repository.
    4. Complete and inspect a local change proposal.
    5. Open Prepare a draft pull request.
    6. Enter the title, description, and optional base branch.
    7. Select Prepare delivery review.
    8. Inspect the exact diff, base, branch, checks, and remote actions.
    9. If the proposal is correct, select Publish this draft PR.

    Preparation creates no remote resource. Publication creates a commit, new branch, and draft pull request. It does not merge.

    Publication can trigger repository workflows. Uncertain publication is not retried automatically. Inspect Publication receipts and GitHub before another action.

    Only github.com is supported. GitHub Enterprise is unavailable.

    Enable bounded Snowflake reads

    Operator setup

    1. Provision an approved read role and token.
    2. Configure SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_JSON in .env.
    3. Restart the application.
    Profile template · no real credential
    SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_JSON='{"A123456":{"account":"org-account","token":"REPLACE_WITH_BEARER_TOKEN","token_type":"OAUTH","role":"DEV_READER","warehouse":"DEV_WH","database":"APP","schema":"PUBLIC","tables":["APP.PUBLIC.EVENTS"]}}'

    Workbench actions

    1. Open Snowflake reads.
    2. Inspect the displayed account, role, warehouse, and allowed tables.
    3. Select Enable these Snowflake reads.
    4. Request schema inspection or a bounded read from an approved table.

    Reads can incur warehouse costs. The connector does not permit arbitrary SQL, joins, data changes, or deployments.

    Each rows request returns at most 100 rows and 20 columns. Token provisioning and renewal remain operator tasks.

    Profiles support org-account account hostnames. Token refresh and signing are unavailable.

    A changed profile invalidates the project's approval. Pending reads are not replayed after a restart.

    Use an ACP-compatible editor
    1. Start the application.
    2. Register the exact repository root in the workbench.
    3. Save editor buffers to disk.
    4. Configure the editor's custom agent command.
    ACP command · use the application's working folder
    /Users/charlie/Repos/deepagents-agents/general-agent/.venv/bin/python -m general_agent.coding.acp --corp-id A123456 --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8001
    1. Set the process working folder to the application folder.
    2. Set the editor's ACP repository folder to the exact registered root.
    3. Start with Plan or Review.
    4. Select Implement when you want a change.
    5. Review the plan permission request.
    6. Review the separate apply permission request after implementation.

    The adapter uses the shared coding service. It does not start a second agent application.

    Answer a pending question in the next editor prompt. The adapter reads saved source, not unsaved buffers.

    No specific editor application has been validated live. Use the workbench for incomplete or binary previews.

    Enable VS Code inline suggestions
    1. Configure INLINE_MODEL_NAME and its provider credential.
    2. Restart the application.
    3. Register the repository and create a coding session.
    4. Open editors/vscode/ in VS Code.
    5. Select Run → Start Debugging.
    6. Open the registered repository in the extension development window.
    7. Trust the workspace.
    8. Set the extension settings below.
    VS Code settings · replace the session identifier
    {
  "generalAgentInline.enabled": true,
  "generalAgentInline.apiUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8001",
  "generalAgentInline.corpId": "A123456",
  "generalAgentInline.sessionId": "REPLACE_WITH_EXISTING_SESSION_ID"
}

    Inline suggestions use a separate model path. They have no tools and do not run coding tasks.

    Accepting a suggestion changes the editor buffer through normal VS Code behavior. It does not prove correctness or save the file.

    Suggestions are disabled by default and can incur provider charges. Reopen documents after a stale source binding or application restart.

    The extension is a development-host setup. Real editor latency and suggestion quality remain unvalidated.

    Source: connector setup and authority · ACP setup · inline extension setup · GitHub controls.

    09

    Resolve a problem

    Read the cause before you repeat an action. Use the logs to choose the next step.

    Common causes and recovery actions.
    What you seePossible causeWhat to do
    The application cannot connect.The API is stopped or the configured API address differs.Inspect the launcher terminal. Start the services. Refresh the page.
    The launcher rejects configuration.Missing model settings, invalid JSON, or a non-loopback host.Correct .env. Single-quote JSON values. Keep loopback addresses.
    A port is already in use.Another service owns the configured port.Stop the known owner or select a free port. Update related URL settings together.
    Implement is unavailable.The selected runtime is not ready.Open Runtime and optional tools. Resolve its error. Use CODING_RUNTIME=local for Docker-free execution.
    A check cannot find a package or tool.A project dependency or host toolchain is missing.Inspect Dependencies. Prepare eligible packages. Have the operator supply the required toolchain.
    Dependency preparation is blocked.Unsupported locks, private/local sources, missing tools, or incompatible engines.Read the blocker. Provide supported locked inputs in a reviewed source change. Create a new session if needed.
    Dependencies show not prepared again.The lockfile or selected runtime identity changed.Prepare the current dependencies. Run checks again.
    TypeScript navigation is unavailable.Node or the exact TypeScript 5.9.3 SDK is missing.Use the SDK setup procedure. Keep the optional SDK path absolute.
    Browser checks are unavailable after restart.The standard launcher removed the browser extra.Use the manual browser startup procedure in chapter 06.
    A preview listener is rejected.The port is occupied, the server binds broadly, or another process owns it.Use a free port and an explicit 127.0.0.1 bind. Start through the agent's preview tool.
    A browser result is stale.Preview source or dependency identity changed.Stop the preview. Start a new preview for the current source. Repeat the browser check.
    The task is waiting_input.The agent needs a decision or missing information.Enter Your answer. Select Answer and resume.
    The task completed but shows not_verified.Required current checks did not pass.Inspect the check logs. Resolve the failure or missing evidence. Request the required checks.
    Apply reports a conflict.The original files or registered root changed after review.Inspect the original. Preserve newer edits. Create a fresh session and review a new proposal.
    Revert refuses the write.The original contains newer edits after application.Inspect both versions. Resolve the change manually. Do not force a stale revision.
    An active task failed after restart.The application abandoned interrupted execution.Inspect partial changes. Select Continue as a new attempt when available.
    GitHub publication is uncertain.A timeout or lost response obscured a remote mutation.Inspect receipts and remote state. Do not repeat publication without review.
    A document cannot render.The required local renderer is absent.Ask the operator to provide the required renderer. Inspect the available output. Record the missing check.

    Stop and continue a coding task

    1. Select Stop task.
    2. Wait for the stopped state.

      The application closes owned command groups and previews. Eligible partial source changes can remain as review evidence.

    3. Inspect the logs and partial diff.
    4. If continuation is required, select Continue as a new attempt.

      The new attempt links to the failed or stopped attempt. It does not silently resume the old shell command.

    The current product cannot change registered project names or check commands. A distinct checkout can register fresh values.

    Documentation domains can change. Finish active project work, then reopen the same absolute root with the required exact hostnames.

    Source: startup checks · recovery controls · recovery and evidence.

    10

    Reference and limits

    Use these terms consistently. Keep the difference between a copy, a check, and an applied change clear.

    Chat workspace
    Live files for one General assistant chat.
    Shared workspace
    Files intentionally retained across chats in one corporation namespace.
    Turn version
    An immutable retained version of a created, changed, or deleted file.
    Project
    A registered original repository root with its check commands and approved documentation domains.
    Session
    A coding workspace that starts from eligible on-disk source and contains its own review copy.
    Attempt
    One queued or running coding task with a mode, budgets, logs, and outcome.
    Check
    A recorded validation command with its result and source/environment identity.
    Change proposal
    An immutable source revision and diff available for review.
    Apply
    The explicit action that writes selected reviewed files to the registered original.
    Preview
    A temporary process using a private source copy. Its writes do not become code proposals.
    Corporation namespace
    The corp_id scope used for application data. It is not authentication or host process isolation.

    What local mode enforces

    • Finite command time and output bounds.
    • Owned process-group cancellation.
    • Validated source inclusion and export caps.
    • Filtered command environments.
    • Scoped application records and immutable evidence.
    • Reviewed root and original-file checks during apply.

    What local mode does not enforce

    • An operating-system sandbox.
    • Host filesystem or network confinement.
    • Container CPU, memory, or process quotas.
    • A host disk quota.
    • Isolation from every native host library or service.
    • Authentication for remote or untrusted users.

    Common default limits

    AreaDefaultMeaning
    Uploads10 files · 100 MiB per fileThe configured upload limits apply to each submission.
    Command / run duration120 seconds / 900 secondsTimeouts bound execution. Task-specific tools can use shorter limits.
    Command output100,000 bytesLong output is truncated. Inspect the retained logs.
    Repository copy50 MiB · 5,000 filesEligible source must fit both configured limits. Each source file is limited to five MiB.
    Model / tool / task calls32 / 64 / 12Shared run admission limits apply to agent and delegated work.
    Reported model tokens1,000,000 per runThe provider must report usage. In-flight calls can overshoot the observed ceiling.
    Coding workers2The durable queue also permits one writer per session.
